name: dtls-context-aware-handshake-message-7a87
instr:
Pion DTLS cannot perform opt-in, context-aware semantic validation of hello and encrypted-extension messages, directly or during DTLS 1.2 and 1.3 handshakes. Implement disabled, observe, and enforce modes with complete structured diagnostics.

Validate every context-dependent contradiction, including initial, retry, version, offered-extension, and negotiated-value semantics. Return all independent issues in deterministic message order. Reports must remain immutable after source mutation. Preserve validation error reports, causes, text, and unwrapping.

Support direct validation of the three concrete message types without a connection. For unsupported Message implementations, return an explicit unsupported-validation result without calling Marshal. Map enforced semantic rejection to the deterministic `illegal_parameter` protocol alert classification.

Apply the policy to clients, servers, listeners, resumed connections, and detached connections. Disabled mode must preserve existing bytes, ordering, errors, and outcomes. Events must be immutable snapshots of direction, role, version, stage, message type, and the complete report. Observe mode must not change structurally accepted flights.

Enforce inbound validation before dependent state. Validate outbound initial and retried ClientHello, ServerHello, and EncryptedExtensions after hooks, with exact negotiated context and emission order, before bytes, transcripts, or dependent progress. Rejection suppresses the message and later
